rpc: cursor-paginate get_address_utxos / get_script_utxos (issue #15 Q5)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/18

## Issue #15 Q5 — fix the silent 1000-UTXO truncation

The `get_address_utxos` / `get_script_utxos` cap was a **correctness bug**, not a UX one: an address (or script) with more than 1000 UTXOs returned only the first 1000 with a `truncated` flag and **no way to fetch the rest**. This replaces the cap with cursor pagination so a caller can walk the full set.

Standalone, independent of the Tier 1 mempool work in #17 — touches only `UtxoSet` and the two read handlers.

### What's here

- **`UtxoSet::utxos_for_script_paged`** — returns up to `limit` mature UTXOs whose `OutPoint` sorts strictly after the cursor, in ascending `OutPoint` order (the `by_script` BTreeSet order). O(scanned) per page; ranges the set rather than re-scanning from the front.
- **`get_address_utxos` / `get_script_utxos`** gain optional `cursor` and `limit` (clamped to `[1, 1000]`) params, and return **`next_cursor`** (`"<tx_id_hex>:<output_index>"`) whenever a full page is returned. Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page.
- **Back-compat:** `truncated` is kept (`= next_cursor.is_some()`); existing single-call clients still work unchanged and now receive a cursor to continue instead of silently losing data past 1000.

### Tests

- `utxos_for_script_paged_walks_full_set_without_dropping` — five UTXOs on one script, paged at `limit=2`, asserts all five surface across pages in ascending order with no duplicates.
- `utxos_for_script_paged_empty_for_unknown_script`.

`cargo test --lib` green (223). Clippy clean on the changed files.

Addresses Q5 of #15. Tier 2 (SSE) and `get_address_history` remain separate follow-ups.
